title: Triangle Removal Process: Exact Asymptotics
description: Formalizes the gap between the Bohman-Frieze-Lubetzky n^{3/2+o(1)} result and the conjectured Θ(n^{3/2}) for the triangle removal process on K_n. Proves structural decompositions, exponent characterizations, and sufficient conditions for the full conjecture.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)

mathlibDependencies.description: G.CliqueFree k means no k-element clique exists.

originalContributions: BFL sandwich theorem combining upper and lower bounds
Exact exponent characterization: 3/2 is the critical exponent
Conjecture decomposition into independent upper/lower Θ-bounds
Sufficient conditions: limit convergence implies full conjecture
Complete graph triangle existence for variable Fin n
Small-value bounds from complete graph edge count
Lower exponent characterization: f exceeds any sub-3/2 power
Mantel/Turan connection via triangle-free terminal graph
Ratio tightness and bounded ratio characterization

references.authors: T. Bohman, A. Frieze, E. Lubetzky
references.title: Random triangle removal

meta.historicalContext: Erdős conjectured that the triangle removal process on K_n leaves Θ(n^{3/2}) edges. Bohman, Frieze, and Lubetzky (2015) proved f(n) = n^{3/2+o(1)}, confirming the exponent but leaving the question of explicit constants open.

sections.title: Triangle Definitions
sections.summary: Defines pointwise triangle predicates and their relationship to Mathlib's CliqueFree 3.

sections.title: Asymptotic Infrastructure
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the triangle removal function f(n) and the BFL/Grable bounds.

sections.title: Gap Analysis: BFL vs Full Conjecture
sections.summary: Proves structural relationships between the BFL result and the full Θ(n^{3/2}) conjecture.

sections.title: Exponent Characterization
sections.summary: Proves 3/2 is the exact critical exponent: any α > 3/2 gives an upper bound, no β < 3/2 works.

sections.title: Sufficient Conditions for the Conjecture
sections.summary: States and partially proves that ratio convergence or limsup/liminf bounds imply the full conjecture.

sections.title: Lower Exponent Characterization
sections.summary: BFL implies f exceeds any sub-3/2 power: for any α < 3/2, eventually n^α ≤ f(n).

sections.title: Mantel/Turan Connection
sections.summary: Connects the triangle removal process to Mantel's theorem via the triangle-free terminal graph. Shows BFL gives n^{7/4} bound, much tighter than Mantel's n²/4.

sections.title: Hierarchy of Bounds
sections.summary: Proves the strict weakening chain: Conjecture ⟹ BFL ⟹ Grable, each step losing information about the multiplicative constant.

sections.title: Tightness and Ratio Characterization
sections.summary: Under the conjecture, the normalized ratio f(n)/n^{3/2} is bounded between positive constants. Characterizes the conjecture as a compactness condition on the ratio sequence.

overview.summary: Analyzes what separates the known BFL result (f(n) = n^{3/2+o(1)}) from the full Erdős conjecture (f(n) = Θ(n^{3/2})). The gap is precisely: BFL gives n^{-ε} ≤ f(n)/n^{3/2} ≤ n^ε (sub-polynomial bounds), while the conjecture needs constant bounds c ≤ f(n)/n^{3/2} ≤ C.
overview.keyIdea: The conjecture decomposes into independent upper and lower Θ-bounds, each equivalent to bounding the ratio f(n)/n^{3/2}. If this ratio converges to any positive limit, the full conjecture follows.
prerequisites: Real power functions and basic inequalities

conclusion.summary: Complete formalization of the structural relationship between BFL's n^{3/2+o(1)} result and Erdős's Θ(n^{3/2}) conjecture. All theorems fully proved (0 sorries). Includes BFL sandwich, exact exponent characterization, conjecture decomposition, Mantel connection, hierarchy of bounds, and ratio tightness characterization.
openQuestions: Does f(n)/n^{3/2} converge? If so, to what constant?
Can the lower Θ-bound be established independently of the upper?
Can differential equation methods (as in BFL) give explicit constants?
